claims.text: The coupled wear-corrosion response of high-entropy alloys is governed by formation of a mechanically mixed layer.
The mechanically mixed layer enhances corrosion protection.
The mechanically mixed layer increases wear through third-body abrasion.
Tribo-corrosion under the proposed conditions forms a mechanically mixed layer.
The mechanically mixed layer acts as a barrier that reduces corrosion current density.
Relative to the stated baseline, corrosion rate will decrease by 20%.
Relative to the stated baseline, wear rate will increase by 30%.
Relative to the stated baseline, total degradation will increase by 10%.
The prediction should hold for CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloys with grain sizes of 10–50 micrometers.
The prediction may fail for alloys with substantially different compositions or microstructures.
Surface roughness, testing conditions, and processing history may affect degradation behavior.

An increase in corrosion rate greater than 10% together with a decrease in wear rate greater than 20% would show that the mechanically mixed layer is not significant in governing the coupled response.

contradictions.description: The baseline is corrosion-only and therefore has no comparable tribological wear rate; a 30% increase in wear rate relative to that baseline is undefined. This also prevents the stated 10% change in total degradation from being interpreted as a matched component-wise comparison.
